tagline: Across mountain gaps to warm mineral pools and the Maury River
intro: Route 39 crosses ridges and follows river valleys between the West Virginia line and East Lexington, with a hairpin on the descent from Ryder Gap and a passage beside the Maury River through Goshen Pass. The entire highway is a Virginia Byway. The Commonwealth designates these scenic roads to introduce travelers to alternative destinations. At Ryder Gap, the state line also divides the James River and Monongahela River watersheds, before the road descends toward the spring settlements.

The corridor links communities that grew around hot springs. At Warm Springs, the men’s pool has an octagonal foundation built in 1761, while its wooden structure was first built in the 1820s. Farther east, Rockbridge Baths gained a resort hotel in 1857. It became a Virginia Military Institute summer school in 1921, then burned in 1926 and was never rebuilt.

Driving east from Ryder Gap, the route follows Back Creek, crosses to the Jackson River and reaches Warm Springs along Warm Springs Run. Beyond Warm Springs Mountain, it follows the Cowpasture River to Millboro Springs, then crosses through Mill Mountain’s gap to Goshen. The Calfpasture rivers unite as the Maury, which carries the drive through Goshen Pass. Continue through Rockbridge Baths toward East Lexington; at Cedar Grove, Route 252 branches toward Brownsburg.

moments.title: Warm Springs Pools
moments.text: The men’s pool house begins with an octagon: its foundation dates to 1761, but the wooden structure above was first built in the 1820s. The women’s pool house, built in 1836, has 22 sides. A mineral spring supplies the pools with 98-degree water. Steam and mineral water gradually damaged the untreated wood, and Bath County ordered the buildings closed in 2017. Rehabilitation began in 2021, using photographs and documents of their 1925 appearance. The pools reopened in December 2022. The men’s spa holds 40,000 gallons of water, with spring water constantly flowing through it.

moments.title: Goshen Pass
moments.text: An anchor and chain stand high above the Maury River at Goshen Pass, part of a memorial to Matthew Fontaine Maury. After his death, his body traveled from Virginia Military Institute in Lexington toward Hollywood Cemetery in Richmond. At his request, the coach stopped in the pass to collect rhododendrons and mountain ivy. The later memorial includes a vertical stone bearing his face and a poem by Margaret Junkin Preston. Route 39 follows the riverbanks through the gorge. The Maury River itself formed the water gap that gives the pass its shape.

moments.title: Rockbridge Baths
moments.text: Rockbridge Baths once had a hotel large enough for 150 to 200 visitors. Built in 1857, it drew Robert E. Lee and Mary Custis Lee as frequent guests. Illness forced its owner, Dr. Samuel Brown Morrison, to leave in 1900, and most patrons followed. After several changes of ownership, Virginia Military Institute took over in 1921 and established a summer school. Fire destroyed the hotel in 1926. It was never rebuilt; VMI closed the school and sold the property. The community lies on Maury River Road, midway between Lexington and Goshen.
